name: Oriente
desc: Digital lending company running consumer credit apps Cashalo in the Philippines and Finmas in Indonesia for underbanked consumers and merchants.
markets: Philippines (Cashalo) and Indonesia (Finmas); offices reported in Singapore, Taipei, Manila, Jakarta, Ho Chi Minh City; Vietnam launch planned, unconfirmed. Sources date from 2018-2020.
rationale: South-East Asian consumer lender with limited brand budget; F1 visibility in Asia is plausible but current scale is unverified.

name: Nakamoto Inc.
desc: Nasdaq-listed bitcoin treasury company, formerly healthcare provider KindlyMD, that holds bitcoin on its balance sheet and is closing legacy clinics.
markets: US-based holding company whose main asset is bitcoin; legacy Utah healthcare clinics being shut; no verified operating markets abroad.
rationale: Investor-facing bitcoin treasury vehicle with no consumer product; F1 sponsorship would offer little commercial return.
changed: KindlyMD merged with Nakamoto Holdings in August 2025; later renamed Nakamoto Inc.

name: Altavair
desc: Commercial aircraft leasing asset manager that buys new and used aircraft and leases them to passenger airlines and cargo operators.
markets: Leases to more than 80 airline customers in about 50 countries per directory profiles; London-based affiliate Altavair Ltd.
rationale: Airline-facing B2B lessor; F1 hospitality could entertain airline clients across many countries, but brand marketing need is small.
changed: KKR agreed in January 2026 to raise its stake in Altavair and sister company AV AirFinance; size of stake not confirmed.

name: Aria
desc: Embedded invoice financing provider that pays suppliers and freelancers early through B2B marketplaces, ERP systems and vertical software platforms.
markets: Works with more than 70 European B2B marketplaces and freelance platforms, including Malt and Job&Talent; scaling invoice financing across Europe.
rationale: European B2B fintech with small marketing budget; F1 offers limited fit beyond niche platform-partner hospitality.

name: Pipe
desc: Embedded capital platform that offers working capital to small businesses inside the software and payment platforms they already use.
markets: Live in the US, Canada, UK and Australia; about a fifth of originations outside the US; expanding partner network globally.
rationale: B2B fintech selling through software partners; F1 could support partner hospitality in US, UK and Australia, but budget is modest.
changed: Pivoted in 2024 from revenue-trading marketplace to embedded capital platform; new CEO Claurelle Rakipovic in December 2025.

name: HashKey Holdings
desc: Digital asset group operating the licensed HashKey Exchange, asset management and blockchain services for retail and institutional crypto investors.
markets: Hong Kong SFC-licensed exchange plus a Bermuda exchange; pursuing licences in Singapore, Dubai, Japan and parts of Europe.
rationale: Crypto exchanges are active F1 sponsors; a newly listed Hong Kong exchange could use F1 to build Asian and global brand awareness.
changed: Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2025.

name: Ethic
desc: SEC-registered investment adviser offering direct indexing, model portfolios and values-based portfolio technology to wealth advisers and their clients.
markets: Serves US wealth advisers as an SEC-registered adviser; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: US B2B wealth technology firm with niche audience; weak F1 fit beyond small adviser hospitality.

name: Lightspark
desc: Payments infrastructure company whose Grid API lets banks, fintechs and businesses send real-time cross-border payments using Bitcoin and stablecoins.
markets: Grid payout network reported in about 65 countries; Revolut Lightning partnership in Europe; Visa card programme across 100+ countries announced 2026.
rationale: Crypto and payments brands are prominent F1 sponsors; F1 could showcase global payments technology to banks and fintech partners.

name: Wealthfront
desc: Online financial platform offering automated investing, high-yield cash accounts, bond and stock tools, and loans to mostly younger US clients.
markets: Serves about 1.3-1.5 million clients in the United States; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Newly listed US consumer fintech chasing young affluent customers; F1's growing US fan base offers a plausible brand-building platform.
changed: IPO on Nasdaq in December 2025; UBS acquisition agreed in 2022 was cancelled.

name: TheStreet
desc: Financial news website publishing market news and stock analysis, with free content and paid subscriptions such as TheStreet Pro.
markets: Audience of US retail investors; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Small US financial media brand owned by a publisher; more likely a media partner than a paying F1 sponsor.
changed: Acquired by TheMaven (renamed The Arena Group in 2021) in August 2019.

name: Billtrust
desc: Accounts receivable automation software provider offering invoicing, credit, payments and cash application tools to B2B suppliers and distributors.
markets: Mainly North American B2B suppliers; offices reported in Poland, India, the Netherlands and Belgium; about 2,600 customers (2023).
rationale: B2B finance software firm; F1 hospitality could entertain enterprise finance buyers, but consumer brand value is low.
changed: Taken private by EQT Private Equity in 2022 (previously BTRS on Nasdaq).

name: Pathstone
desc: Independent multi-family office and wealth management firm advising wealthy families, family offices and institutions on investments and planning.
markets: US wealthy families and institutions through offices including Englewood NJ and the Philadelphia area; no verified international operations.
rationale: US wealth manager whose high-net-worth clients suit F1 hospitality, but domestic focus limits sponsorship scale.
changed: Combined with Mill Creek Capital Advisors effective June 2026; a planned merger with Hall Capital was reported, status not confirmed.

name: CI Financial
desc: Wealth and asset manager running CI Global Asset Management and CI Wealth in Canada, US firm Corient, and Australian funds.
markets: Asset and wealth management in Canada, US wealth management through Corient, and asset management in Australia.
rationale: Wealth manager serving affluent clients in Canada, US and Australia, all F1 host markets; hospitality value plausible.
changed: Taken private by Mubadala Capital in August 2025 and delisted from the TSX (formerly CIX).

name: Forgent Power Solutions
desc: Designer and manufacturer of electrical distribution equipment for data centres, power grids and energy-intensive industrial facilities.
markets: Supplies US data centre, utility and industrial customers; no verified international sales or expansion plans.
rationale: Fast-growing listed supplier to AI data centres; F1 could serve B2B hospitality, but US-only industrial buyer base limits fit.
changed: IPO on the NYSE in February 2026; Neos Partners retained majority voting control at IPO and later sold further shares.

name: Velo3D
desc: Metal additive manufacturing company selling Sapphire laser powder bed fusion printers and parts production for aerospace, defence and energy customers.
markets: Mainly US aerospace and defence customers; European headquarters and technology centre in Augsburg, Germany; targeting UK, Germany, France, Italy.
rationale: Additive manufacturing is used by F1 teams; Velo3D could showcase technology, though rivals like Stratasys already sponsor and budget is small.
changed: Left the NYSE for OTC trading, majority stake acquired by Arrayed Additive, later uplisted to Nasdaq Capital Market.

name: Atomic Machines
desc: Deep-tech manufacturer developing the Matter Compiler, an AI-driven system that builds micro-electromechanical devices such as relays directly from code.
markets: Early-stage; offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara, California; first device PrimeSwitch relay announced October 2026; no verified customers or international activity.
rationale: Newly unveiled deep-tech startup with no established market; F1 technology showcase is conceivable but premature.

name: AssetWatch
desc: Condition monitoring company selling wireless vibration, temperature, oil and motor current sensors with analytics to detect industrial machinery faults.
markets: US manufacturers with nationwide US-based support engineers; some staff in Ontario, Canada; no verified international customer base or expansion plans.
rationale: US industrial IoT supplier selling to plant reliability teams; F1 offers limited commercial benefit beyond niche technology storytelling.

name: Arris Composites
desc: Advanced manufacturer using additive molding to make continuous carbon-fibre composite parts for consumer electronics, footwear, drones, automotive and aerospace.
markets: US production in Berkeley plus operations in Taiwan and Malaysia; customers include Brooks Running and Skydio; Japanese automotive collaboration explored with Chuo Malleable Iron.
rationale: Lightweight carbon-fibre manufacturing fits F1's engineering story; a technology supplier tie-in is plausible but marketing budget is small.

name: Tiendas 3B (BBB Foods)
desc: Mexican hard-discount grocery chain selling food, beverages, cleaning and personal hygiene products, largely private label, through thousands of neighbourhood stores.
markets: Operates about 3,765 stores in Mexico (September 2026), opening hundreds more each year; no stores outside Mexico.
rationale: Fast-growing NYSE-listed Mexican retailer; Mexico City Grand Prix offers domestic brand exposure, but value shoppers are a weak fit for F1.

name: Growve
desc: Brand aggregator that acquires and runs natural supplement, body care, food, household and pet brands sold mainly through online marketplaces.
markets: Mainly US online sales from US plants and offices; owns New Zealand brand The Organic Skin Co.; 2026 Coupang job ad indicates South Korea sales.
rationale: Portfolio of small online brands with no single flagship; F1 sponsorship makes little commercial sense.
changed: Palm Beach Capital led a majority investment; brand count fell from 25+ (2021) to about 15 (2026).

name: MAV Beauty Brands
desc: Personal care company owning hair, face and body brands Marc Anthony True Professional, Renpure, Cake Beauty and The Mane Choice.
markets: Its four brands sell in more than 25 countries (2023); specific countries not stated.
rationale: Mass-market hair care owner recently restructured under private equity; limited budget makes F1 a weak fit.
changed: Entered CCAA creditor protection in November 2023; assets sold to Nexus Capital Management in December 2023; delisted from the TSX.

name: Pacific World Corporation
desc: Nail and beauty products maker known for Nailene artificial nails, supplying nail and foot care items to drugstores and retailers.
markets: US retail customers; 2011 acquisition described as making it a top global nail care player; reported 2024 purchase of UK brand Nails.INC, unverified.
rationale: Mass-market nail care maker with little brand marketing at sponsorship scale; weak F1 fit.
changed: Bought by Levine Leichtman Capital Partners; later reported as a wholly owned subsidiary of Prospect Capital (aggregator source).
